description: A mathematically-inclined student interested in Data Science who enjoys the theoretical side of CS but feels less confident about low-level C++ implementation and memory management.

nodes.title: C++ Classes and Templates
nodes.description: Introduction to C++ syntax, class structures, and template basics within the Goodrich textbook context.
nodes.personalizationRationale: As a student with some prior exposure to C++, this core node solidifies existing knowledge of object-oriented design before moving to complex structures.

nodes.title: Memory Management: Pointers vs. References
nodes.description: Deep dive into the distinction between pointers, references, and manual memory management in C++.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Because the student has some prior exposure but not full mastery, this single scaffolding node clarifies pointer-reference nuances often skipped in intro courses.

nodes.title: Linked List Implementation
nodes.description: Implementing singly and doubly linked lists and analyzing their performance.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This node provides the fundamental list implementation requirements for students with some prior exposure to programming.

nodes.description: Recursive algorithm design and Big-O asymptotic analysis for time and space complexity.
nodes.title: Quiz 1: Recursion & Analysis
nodes.personalizationRationale: This assessment ensures the student with some prior exposure can apply Big-O notation to recursion, a key course objective.

nodes.title: Stacks and Queues
nodes.description: Abstract Data Types for Stacks and Queues using C++ templates.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Building on some prior exposure, this core node focuses on implementing standard ADTs using C++ class templates.

nodes.description: Usage and implementation of dynamic arrays (Vectors) and Iterator patterns.
nodes.title: Vectors and Iterators
nodes.personalizationRationale: Essential for students with some prior exposure to understand how C++ handles dynamic resizing and sequence traversal.

nodes.title: Sequences and Bubble Sort
nodes.description: Implementation of Bubble Sort and its efficiency within sequence-based structures.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core requirement for understanding early sorting algorithms, tailored for a student with some prior exposure.
This mandatory assessment ensures the student with some prior exposure is fully prepared for the midterm exam.
nodes.title: Midterm Review Assessment
nodes.description: Comprehensive review of blocks 1-3 material including memory, lists, and complexity analysis.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Core tree concepts that build on the recursive foundations established for students with some prior exposure.
nodes.description: Definitions and traversal algorithms (Pre-order, Post-order) for general tree structures.
nodes.title: General Tree Traversals

nodes.personalizationRationale: Required core knowledge of binary structures for students with some prior exposure.
nodes.description: Properties and implementations of binary trees, including linked and array-based representations.
nodes.title: Binary Tree Foundations

nodes.description: Implementing priority queues using binary heaps and analyzing heap-sort components.
nodes.title: Priority Queues and Heaps
nodes.personalizationRationale: Heaps are a key requirement; this node targets the student's existing some_prior_exposure to refine their heap-logic implementation.
Essential core content for students with some prior exposure, focusing on the efficiency of hash-based lookups.
nodes.description: Hash functions, collision resolution strategies, and the Map ADT.
nodes.title: Maps and Hash Tables
Quiz 3: Maps and Dictionaries
nodes.description: Assessment of hash functions and dictionary implementation performance.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory quiz checkpoint to verify the student's mastery of dictionary structures given their some_prior_exposure.
Provides the necessary core theory on balanced trees for students with some prior exposure.
nodes.description: Binary Search Tree (BST) operations and AVL tree rotation logic for balancing.
nodes.title: BST and AVL Trees

nodes.description: Properties and maintenance of Red-Black trees and (2,4) multi-way search trees.
nodes.title: Red-Black and Multi-Way Trees
nodes.personalizationRationale: Advanced tree theory required for the final exam, designed for students with some prior exposure to complex logic.

nodes.description: Divide-and-conquer sorting (Merge Sort) vs. simple Selection Sort analysis.
nodes.title: Merge Sort & Selection Sort
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core sorting algorithms that every student, including those with some prior exposure, must master for the capstone.

nodes.description: Investigation into hybrid sorting techniques like Timsort (used in Python/Java) and their C++ equivalents.
nodes.title: Advanced Sorting: Hybrid Techniques
nodes.personalizationRationale: Since the student has some prior exposure, this enrichment node connects course concepts to real-world language implementations they may have seen.

nodes.description: Cumulative review of all data structures, algorithms, and C++ memory patterns for the final exam.
nodes.title: Final Exam Review Point
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory cumulative review to ensure the student with some prior exposure is ready for the final exam.
